meta.description: Free topographic map of Switzerland and Liechtenstein for Garmin handhelds, with routing, based on swisstopo data.

hero.eyebrow: Garmin map · Free of charge · Routable
hero.title: Based on the swisstopo national map – for your Garmin
hero.lead: Free topographic map of Switzerland and Liechtenstein for Garmin GPSMAP, Montana, eTrex, epix, fēnix and others<sup>1</sup> as well as BaseCamp, based on open data from swisstopo, with hiking trails, contour lines, address search and routing on foot and by bike.
dl.title: Downloads
dl.lead: Besides the vector map, there is the pixel map with the familiar map image in three levels of detail, and the aerial image in two.
features.title: What the map offers
features.lead: Built from swisstopo's open geodata for Switzerland and Liechtenstein, in the style of the 1:25,000 national map.
f1.h: In the style of the national map
f1.p: Colours, lines and labels in the style of the 1:25,000 national map.
f2.p: Routes on foot and by bike, calculated right on your Garmin.
f3.p: Hiking trails by category plus cycling, mountain bike and skating routes from SwitzerlandMobility.
f4.p: Contour lines and spot heights from the swissALTI3D elevation model, as an overlay you can switch on.
f5.p: Search by street and house number (Switzerland), places, peaks, passes and stations.
f6.p: Free of charge, no account needed. Every release follows swisstopo's new data versions, and the data version is shown with every download.

inst.title: Onto your Garmin in three steps
inst.lead: For GPSMAP, Montana, eTrex, epix, fēnix and other Garmin devices with map support.
usb1.h: Download the file for your Garmin
usb1.p: Under Downloads, save the IMG file of the vector map and, for hiking trails and cycle routes, the routes overlay. No need to rename them.
usb2.p: Connect it via USB. It shows up as a drive; ideally use the microSD card.
usb3.p: Eject your Garmin and restart it. In the map settings, enable only one background map (vector map, pixel map or aerial image) plus the routes overlay. If several background maps are active, your Garmin draws them all on top of each other and the display slows down.
bc1.p: Under Downloads, choose the BaseCamp package (ZIP) and unzip it.
bc2.p: Copy the folder ending in .gmap: on Windows to C:\ProgramData\Garmin\Maps\, on macOS to ~/Library/Application Support/Garmin/Maps/.
bc3.p: The map then appears under “Maps”. Plan routes and send them to your Garmin.
faq.title: Frequently asked questions
q1.q: Is this an official map from swisstopo or Garmin?
q1.a: No. It is an independent project that provides the open geodata of swisstopo (OGD) and SwitzerlandMobility (Open Data) in the Garmin map format (IMG). Unofficial conversion, not published by swisstopo.
q2.a: So far the map has only been tested on the GPSMAP and in BaseCamp. Montana, eTrex, epix, fēnix and other Garmin devices with map support read the same IMG format and should work as well.
q3.q: What is the difference between the vector and the raster map?
q3.a: The vector map is compact, searchable and routable. The pixel map shows the image of the national map at several scales, depending on the variant from 1:10,000, 1:25,000 or 1:50,000 up to 1:1 million. As you zoom, it switches automatically to the matching scale. It cannot route.
q4.q: Can I use it for car navigation?
q4.a: Only to a limited extent. The map knows roads and road classes, but not turn restrictions. Routing is meant for walking and cycling; for driving it is at most good for rough orientation.
q5.a: Every release states the data version of the datasets used. New releases come out when swisstopo publishes new data.
q6.a: Send an email to blog_papyri8c@icloud.com. Give the location and the zoom level and attach a screenshot. If you have a GitHub account, you can also open an issue.

dl.fat32: Every file for your Garmin is under 4 GB and fits on FAT32 memory cards. The BaseCamp packages cover all of Switzerland and can be larger.
q7.q: Is this related to Garmin TOPO Switzerland?
q7.a: No. This map is an independent project and has nothing to do with Garmin's paid maps such as TOPO Schweiz v2 PRO. It is free of charge, and every release states the data version of the swisstopo data used.
q10.a: The geodata from swisstopo is open and free. So we turn it into a map for Garmin devices and pass it on for free as well. Helvetopo uses the current swisstopo data and states the data version with every release. The vector map has street names, address search and routing for walking and cycling. The raster map switches to the matching scale as you zoom, from the detailed map up to 1:1,000,000.
q11.q: What’s the catch? Nothing is free.
q11.a: There is no catch. Helvetopo has no commercial interest: no ads, no trackers or analytics, no cookies, no account, no paid version. The web server and the download storage log only what operation technically requires (details in the privacy policy). The project comes from a love of good maps and of swisstopo’s map series.
q8.a: Yes. The swisstopo data also covers Liechtenstein: terrain, roads, paths, names and contour lines. Address search, however, is only available for Switzerland, because the official register of building addresses contains Swiss addresses only.

q9.q: When does my Garmin show which scale of the pixel map?
q9.a:
Each pixel map contains several scales. As you zoom, your Garmin switches automatically to the matching scale. With the map detail setting “Normal”, the mapping is roughly as follows (zoom display on the Garmin, measured on a GPSMAP 67):

Zoom10-100025-100050-1000
up to approx. 120 m1:10,0001:25,0001:50,000
approx. 200–300 m1:25,0001:25,0001:50,000
approx. 500–800 m1:50,0001:50,0001:50,000
approx. 1.2 km1:100,0001:100,0001:100,000
approx. 2–3 km1:200,0001:200,0001:200,000
approx. 5 km1:500,0001:500,0001:500,000
approx. 8 km1:1 million1:1 million1:1 million

Below approx. 120 m, Garmin has no further levels. If you zoom in further, your Garmin only enlarges the image. That is why 1:10,000 appears only at a very strong zoom.

The map detail setting shifts the changes by one level:

  • “Less”: your Garmin switches earlier to the coarser scale. This helps if the map looks too small or too fine.
  • “More”: the finer scale stays on screen longer.

On the GPSMAP 66/67, according to the manual, the setting is under map page → MENU → Map Setup → Advanced Setup → Map Detail. The labels can differ by device and language.

The planned aerial image behaves the same way. Because the photo is very fine (approx. 0.6 m per pixel), it stays sharp longer when enlarged.
q14.q: Why do I see the public transport stops on the GPSMAP only when I zoom in (approx. 80 m)?
q14.a: Your Garmin decides itself from which zoom it shows a point. This limit depends on the type of the point. For the stops in the route overlay, the limit on the GPSMAP 67 is approx. 80 m. We tested other point types and settings. With them, the stops did not reliably appear earlier on the device. At 80 m there is also enough space for the names of the stops. BaseCamp on the computer shows the stops earlier. The vector map shows the railway stations from approx. 200 m.
q12.q: Why aren’t the pixel map and aerial image a single file for all of Switzerland?
q12.a: Your Garmin reads maps from memory cards formatted as FAT32, where a single file can be at most 4 GB. Compact and the Standard aerial image fit into one file. The more detailed variants are larger for all of Switzerland, so they come in two halves (West and East) or per region. Download the areas you need and copy them all into the Garmin folder. BaseCamp on your computer has no such limit, so there is one package for all of Switzerland.
priv.title: Datenschutzerklärung
priv.body:
Helvetopo ist ein privates, nicht kommerzielles Projekt. Hier steht, welche Daten beim Besuch dieser Seite und beim Herunterladen der Karten anfallen.

Kontakt

Verantwortlich ist der Betreiber von Helvetopo. Kontakt: blog_papyri8c@icloud.com

Die Kontaktadresse liegt bei iCloud Mail von Apple, einem Anbieter ausserhalb Europas (USA). Wenn du eine E-Mail schreibst, verarbeitet Apple diese Nachricht. Für das Herunterladen und Benutzen der Karten brauchst du keine E-Mail.

Wo die Daten liegen

Portal, Downloads und die Dokumentation zu jedem Release laufen ausschliesslich auf Servern in Europa. Der Webserver steht bei einem Hosting-Anbieter in Deutschland. Die Kartendateien liegen auf einem Speicher in der Schweiz und gehen verschlüsselt über den Webserver an dich.

Was der Webserver protokolliert

Bei jedem Aufruf speichert der Webserver:

  • die gekürzte IP-Adresse (IPv4 ohne die letzte Zahl, IPv6 nur die ersten 48 Bit)
  • Datum und Uhrzeit
  • die aufgerufene Adresse, den Statuscode und die übertragene Datenmenge
  • die verweisende Seite (Referrer) und die Kennung des Browsers (User-Agent)

Bei technischen Fehlern schreibt der Webserver zusätzlich ein Fehlerprotokoll. Es kann die vollständige IP-Adresse enthalten.

Zweck ist der sichere Betrieb: Fehler finden und Missbrauch abwehren. Rechtsgrundlage ist das berechtigte Interesse am sicheren Betrieb (Art. 6 Abs. 1 lit. f DSGVO). Alle Protokolle werden nach 7 Tagen automatisch gelöscht. Wir werten sie nicht zu Profilen aus und geben sie nicht weiter.

Was nicht stattfindet

  • keine Cookies
  • keine Tracker und keine Analyse-Dienste
  • keine Schriften, Skripte oder Bilder von fremden Servern
  • kein Konto und keine Anmeldung

Deine Wahl von Sprache und Farbschema speichert dein Browser lokal (localStorage). Diese Angabe verlässt dein Gerät nicht.

Hosting

Den Webserver betreibt ein Hosting-Anbieter in Deutschland in unserem Auftrag (Auftragsverarbeiter). Er nutzt die Daten nicht für eigene Zwecke.

Links zu anderen Diensten

Der Link „Quellcode (GitHub)“ führt zu GitHub in den USA. Diesen Dienst brauchen nur Personen, die Helvetopo selbst bauen oder mitentwickeln. Links zu Garmin führen ebenfalls zu Diensten ausserhalb dieser Seite, teils in den USA. Dort gelten deren Datenschutzbestimmungen. Diese Seite lädt nichts von dort.

Deine Rechte

Du kannst Auskunft, Berichtigung, Löschung und Einschränkung verlangen und der Verarbeitung widersprechen. Schreib dafür an die Kontaktadresse. Weil die IP-Adressen gekürzt sind, können wir Protokolleinträge meist keiner Person zuordnen. Du kannst dich auch bei einer Aufsichtsbehörde beschweren, in der Schweiz beim EDÖB.

Stand: November 2026

q13.q: Do I need GitHub or a service outside Europe?
q13.a: No. To download and use the maps, everything runs on servers in Europe (Switzerland and EU): the portal, the downloads and the documentation for each release. You only need GitHub if you want to build Helvetopo yourself or help develop it. The source code is there. The map files are never on GitHub.
